playbooks.label: Monthly WIP review
playbooks.summary: Lines up each job's contract, estimated cost, percent complete and billing from the month's close, so the president, project managers and accounting can review margins and over and under billing.

playbooks.label: Change order approval
playbooks.summary: Collects each change order's price and backup and routes it for approval inside the company before it goes to the owner for signature.

playbooks.label: Bid coverage check
playbooks.summary: Lists the bids due and, for each trade, how many subcontractor quotes are in, so the estimator can chase the gaps before the deadline.

playbooks.label: Monthly pay applications
playbooks.summary: Puts each subcontractor pay application next to its subcontract for the project manager's review, then checks the lien waiver and insurance before payment.

playbooks.label: Weekly open items
playbooks.summary: Pulls open RFIs and submittals, who has each one, and the scheduled work waiting on them, ahead of the weekly owner and subcontractor meetings.

playbooks.label: Subcontractor insurance check
playbooks.summary: Checks every line on each subcontractor's certificate of insurance for its expiration date and flags lapses before payment.

playbooks.label: Daily log
playbooks.summary: Records the day's weather, manpower by company, equipment, visitors, deliveries and delays, and turns field notes into a draft RFI.

questions.ask: Can we pay a subcontractor whose insurance certificate has lapsed?
questions.reply: No. Accounting holds payment to a subcontractor with a lapsed line until a current certificate is on file, and tells the project manager and superintendent the same day. The section from the subcontractor insurance procedure is in the panel, with the payment steps from the monthly billing procedure.
questions.before: Finding the company's own rule meant knowing which procedure to open, or asking someone who did.
questions.now: The answer comes from the company's own procedure, with the section shown.

result.query: lapsed certificate subcontractor holds payment current

results.heading: When a certificate lapses
results.text:
## When a certificate lapses

If any line on a subcontractor's certificate has lapsed, accounting holds payment to that subcontractor until a current certificate is on file, and tells the project manager and superintendent the same day.

results.heading: Before a subcontractor is paid
results.text:
## Before a subcontractor is paid

Accounting pays an approved pay application once the lien waiver for that payment is in and the subcontractor's certificate of insurance is current. Lien waiver forms depend on the state the project is in. Accounting picks the form, and nothing the assistant drafts is signed or sent as a lien waiver.

results.heading: Before a subcontractor starts
results.text:
## Before a subcontractor starts

Every subcontractor sends a certificate of insurance before starting work on site. It shows each line of coverage the subcontract requires, with Tallowbrook Builders as certificate holder, and the additional insured endorsements for ongoing and completed operations attached.

result.query: daily log record weather manpower deliveries delays due

results.heading: What goes in the daily log
results.text:
## What goes in the daily log

Every day there is work on site, the superintendent records in the daily log: the weather, manpower by company, equipment on site, visitors, deliveries, delays and what caused them, inspections, and photos.

results.heading: What stays out of the log
results.text:
## What stays out of the log

Record that an incident happened and who was told. Injury details, first aid and medical information do not go in the daily log; they go to the safety manager.

results.heading: When it is due
results.text:
## When it is due

Each day's log is finished before the superintendent leaves site. Once saved, an entry is not edited; add a note to the next day's log instead.
